sections.title: Name and recognition
sections.text: Russula atroglauca Einhell. is the name accepted by the nomenclatural databases consulted; the taxon was described in 1980. This European brittlegill forms a cap about 3–6 cm across, sometimes up to 8 cm, convex at first, then flattening and often becoming slightly depressed at the centre. Colours range from dark grey-green or olive to blue-green, often with a darker centre; the dry surface is matte, sometimes velvety or pruinose, and may bear rusty spots. The gills are cream and the stem is white, cylindrical or slightly tapered, sometimes rust-spotted near the base. Field descriptions report pale flesh and a mild taste, but these characters are not sufficient for identification.

sections.title: Habitat and status
sections.text: This is an ectomycorrhizal fungus associated with trees. European sources report it with birch, spruce and aspen; host records vary by region. It fruits on soil in woodland, in summer or autumn. Records are scattered, and it may be confused with Russula parazurea, making records and identification challenging.

sections.title: Identification limits and caution
sections.text: Cap colour varies and may be altered by lighting or photo white balance. Other grey-green brittlegills look similar; reliable determination may require examination of spores and cap cuticle, as well as chemical reactions. The sources consulted do not justify a food recommendation: do not eat a specimen based on this entry or image.

traits: Cap convex at first, then flat or slightly depressed; dark grey-green to blue-green, often darker at the centre
Surface matte, sometimes velvety-pruinose; rusty spots may occur
Cream gills; white stem, sometimes rust-spotted at the base
Ectomycorrhizal woodland fungus reported with Betula, Picea and Populus depending on region
Poorly documented European species, including lookalike Russula parazurea
safetyNote: Descriptive entry, not a foraging guide. Grey-green brittlegills can be difficult to distinguish; do not eat based on a photograph or this summary.
